summary: A stuck student conflates the failed 1923 Munich Putsch with Hitler's legal appointment as Chancellor in 1933 and works toward untangling how each event actually connects to the Nazis gaining power.
student_turns: I'm revising Weimar and Nazi Germany and I keep getting the Munich Putsch mixed up with when Hitler actually became Chancellor, I think I've basically been treating them as the same event.
I had it in my head that the Beer Hall Putsch happened in 1933 when Hitler became Chancellor, but I think that might be wrong.
I do know the Putsch failed and Hitler got sent to prison, that's where he wrote Mein Kampf isn't it.
So if the Putsch didn't actually work, how did he end up in power then, was that a totally different event?
Is Hindenburg the one who makes him Chancellor? I always blank on his name when I'm writing under timed conditions.

summary: A discouraged student overwhelmed by the volume of Cold War events works toward understanding the causes behind the Cuban Missile Crisis rather than just listing what happened.
student_turns: I've got a test on the Cold War tomorrow and there's just so many events, I don't know how I'm meant to remember all of them.
I keep mixing up the Berlin Blockade and the Berlin Wall going up, they're both about Berlin and I always end up writing the wrong one under pressure.
I got a really low mark on my last practice essay and my teacher wrote that I was just listing events instead of explaining them, I don't even really get what the difference is.
Could you help me actually understand why the Cuban Missile Crisis happened rather than just what happened, because I think I'd remember it better if I understood the reasons behind it.
Do you reckon I can actually get better at this before the exam or am I just behind everyone else at this point.

summary: An exam-skills session working through how to structure a 16-mark essay on the Elizabethan England depth study.
student_turns: I've got a 16 mark question coming up on Elizabethan England and I don't really know how to structure it, do I just write down everything I know?
My teacher said something about weighing up both sides of the argument but I'm not sure what that actually looks like when you're writing it.
How many paragraphs should I actually be aiming for, I always run out of time and end up rushing the ending.
Do I need a proper conclusion or is that just wasting time I could spend getting more points down?
What's a good example I could use if it was a question about how much of a threat Mary Queen of Scots really was to Elizabeth?
